dedupe_keys.name: fao diem eve global flood monitoring flood persistence cropland and population exposure

description: The DIEM Events Visualization in Emergencies (EVE) system from FAO helps users understand flood events and their impact on different land cover types, with a focus on agricultural areas. It provides a flood persistence analysis and an estimate of the population exposed, using NOAA VIIRS satellite flood data at 375 m resolution and the ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 land cover, for about 40 countries with daily and biweekly updates. On the Humanitarian Data Exchange FAO publishes a global flood events CSV and one CSV per country, covering January 2024 to the present and updated every two weeks, under CC BY, with an EVE user guide. Caveats: FAO notes that EVE relies on global datasets that cannot always capture national or local specificities, that it cannot tell whether flooded cropland was being cultivated at the time, and that it does not distinguish hazardous from non-hazardous floods. It is useful for near-real-time flood hazard exposure of agricultural and rural infrastructure, emergency response targeting and building event histories for resilience analysis; a related record is the FloodScan dataset on HDX.
